main_text.l: prorsus caret. Etenim caloris, frigoris, fic-
citatis & humiditatis, quæ omnium corpo-
ris mutationum primariæ sunt causæ, cœ-
lum expers est. Propterea Aristoteles libro
primo de Cœlo, cœlestia corpora ait esse
incorruptibilia. Præterea
si spiritus diuinū
corpus & cœlestè esset, profecto nullū in-
teriret animal: Propterea quòd animæ & corp-
oris vinculum, quod spiritum vocat Fer-
nelius: esset indissolubile & æternum: At o-
mnia animalia esse mortalia, ne homo qui-
dem ullus, quantumuis brutus negare po-
test. Igitur spiritus, non est cœleste corpus,
sed potiùs vaporosa quædam substantia, ani-
mata, qua nostrum corpus, ut communi in-
strumento ad universas actiones suas ob-
eundas utitur: nec etiam à cœlo originem
ducit, sed
à quatuor mundi elementis. Quod
fane oftedit philosophus decima quæstio-
ne, vicesimæ primæ Sectionis, ubi largiore
humorem, spiritum
item idem largiore parere
ait. Quod etiam libro de spiritu his verbis
confirmare videtur. Aliter (inquit) spiritus
attractione quapiam e venis facta, &
coctione: quando languis extremū, atq; idem
universis est alimentum. Idem porro sanis
testatur uinū syncope correptis, propinatum,

page.notes: Page is in Latin with a few words of doubtful reading in the transcription; the last line ends with a catchword-like word "tum," which is printed as the closing word of the last line and treated as text. Some spellings (e.g. "vinculum", "uocar", "quaestione") are as printed; the transcription above normalises u/v and i/j per the rules, but several words in the scan are hard to read at this resolution and should be checked against the original: "uinculum", "uocar", "Fer-nelius", "spiritum", and the line "Aristoteles libro primo". Lines near the middle contain possibly misprinted or unclear letters; mark: "decima quæstione" and "idem largiore parere" are uncertain.
